correctness.rationale: For arbitrary compact full-dimensional K containing 0, the exact scalar Jensen gap identity yields nonnegativity. Almost-everywhere radial gauge differentiation with uniform translation Lipschitz bounds gives ∫rho0^n t_x²=Q_K(x)+o(|x|²). The uniform lower bound D_p(x)≳p|x|²/(1+p|x|) localizes all three level-set scales. Taylor expansion for p|x|≪1 gives the fine quadratic limit and fixed-p Peano coefficient (n+p)/8; at x=y/p the scalar expansion yields Phi_K; at coarser scale the O(1/p) comparison to ordinary covariogram yields H_K. Local uniform convergence plus coercivity and radial monotonicity gives whole-set Hausdorff. Independent numerical integration on the nonsmooth square at p=2 gives D(h,0)/h²→2=(n+p)Q_K(e1)/8. No C2-neighborhood assertion.
residual_risks: No uniform rate over varying K; a.e. gauge differentiability and geometric localization are the critical general steps, not established by square quadrature alone.
